items.answer: Ideally, virtual reality (VR) software should let a developer provide only high-level descriptions from which all low-level details are automatically determined; the developer can then use middleware between the developer and the hardware, following well-known patterns and calling well-designed software libraries to avoid micro-level activities; and the software should also allow the developer to design functions from scratch for original work rather than depending on middleware.

Human factors in system design requires designers to know the users' characteristics and design the system accordingly, because users who perform the same broad task, such as a traveler or agent and a database administrator obtaining railway ticket information, can have different expectations, needs, and query-language skills, and therefore require different interfaces for providing input, seeing the outcome, and acting on the outcome.

The user-centric approach, generally recommended for building interactive systems, is the process of designing computer systems in which users' needs and expectations are taken care of by considering user characteristics, and it starts by understanding user characteristics, what users need and expect, and then designing the system based on that.
Augmented reality on the reality-virtuality continuum is the intermediate state in which the real environment is augmented with virtual content.

Virtual reality (VR) is, according to the Miriam Webster dictionary, an artificial environment experienced through sensory stimuli, in which sights and sounds play a primary role and are provided by a computer, possibly along with other sensory stimuli, and in which a person's actions partially determine what happens in the environment.
Virtual reality (VR) hardware has three major components: displays (output devices), sensors (input devices), and computers (processing devices).

questions.question: Why might designers use the novice, intermittent, and expert user classes instead of always beginning with empirical or field studies?
options: Because field studies are inexpensive and usually require no elaborate planning
Because field studies are time-consuming and require elaborate planning, while the classes give a design starting point
Because users in all three classes behave exactly the same way
Because the three classes are the only possible user categorization
questions.explanation: Empirical or field studies can be time-consuming, laborious, and require elaborate setup and planning. The novice, intermittent, and expert classes give a broad starting point when the design process starts.

questions.question: In the novice, intermittent, and expert user categorization, what does an expert user mean?
options: A person who uses the system only for the first time
A person who uses the system only occasionally
A person with advanced technical knowledge about system hardware
A person who is an expert in using the system and can use it efficiently
questions.explanation: An expert user is not a technology expert but a person who is an expert in using the system and can use it efficiently.

questions.question: Which user class uses an interactive system occasionally?
options: The expert user
The intermittent user
The technology expert
The novice user
questions.explanation: The three-class classification includes novice users who use the system for the first time, intermittent users who use it occasionally, and expert users who use it regularly over a long period.

questions.question: For a novice first-time user saving a file, why might a menu option be preferred over a hotkey combination?
options: Because menu options are faster than hotkey combinations
Because remembering hotkey combinations is generally difficult for them
Because novices cannot see menu options on a display
Because hotkeys are always preferable for novice users
questions.explanation: A menu option may take longer than a hotkey combination, but it is suitable for novice first-time users because remembering hotkey combinations is generally difficult for them.

questions.question: Why can a word processing or similar application provide both a hotkey combination and a menu option for the same task?
options: To cater to different user groups
To make the menu option unavailable for first-time users
To force intermittent users to use the same option as experts
To reduce the number of ways the task can be performed
questions.explanation: An application can provide multiple options for the same task, such as a hotkey combination and a menu option, to cater to different user groups.

data.text: Interactive-system designers can rely on novice, intermittent, and expert user categorization as a starting point for design decisions instead of always beginning with time-consuming and laborious field studies. This classification distinguishes users by how regularly they use the system, where an expert is defined by system efficiency rather than general technology expertise. Because users in different classes are likely to behave differently, this broad categorization is useful when the design process starts.
points: Designers can rely on novice, intermittent, and expert user categorization instead of always starting with time-consuming and laborious field studies.
Users can be classified into three categories: novice users, intermittent users, and expert users.
An expert user is defined as someone who can use the system efficiently rather than a general technology expert.
These categories provide a starting point for design decisions because users in different classes are likely to behave differently.
This broad categorization is useful when the design process starts, even though more fine-grained categorizations are possible.

questions.question: For an electronic engineer, what does user-centric design mainly concern?
options: A software development lifecycle that accounts for users' needs
The physical form of the product, namely its shape, size, and look
Creative design of interface elements and layouts
Hardware-level features such as more sensors, smaller chips, and a more power-efficient battery
questions.explanation: For an electronic engineer, user-centric design concerns hardware-level features, such as more sensors, smaller chips to reduce size, and a more power-efficient battery.

questions.question: How does an application software developer building a VR or AR system incorporate user characteristics?
options: By following a development lifecycle that accounts for users' characteristics, needs, and expectations
By specifying the physical shape, size, and look of the product
By designing the interface elements and layouts of the system
By adding more sensors, smaller chips, and a power-efficient battery
questions.explanation: An application software developer incorporates user characteristics by following a development or design lifecycle that accounts for users' characteristics, needs, and expectations.

data.text: The meaning of user-centric design varies by stakeholder, whether it concerns interface elements, product form, or hardware features. Application software developers incorporate user characteristics by following a development lifecycle that accounts for user needs and expectations. This ensures the system is easier to use and better matches the users' needs and expectations.
points: The meaning of user-centric design varies depending on the designer's specific role.
Software developers use a development lifecycle that accounts for user characteristics, needs, and expectations.

questions.question: Which three measures are used to evaluate usability?
options: Effectiveness, efficiency, and satisfaction
Effectiveness, efficiency, and control
Effectiveness, efficiency, and functionality
Effectiveness, efficiency, and interaction
questions.explanation: The three measures of usability are effectiveness, efficiency, and satisfaction.

questions.question: In the ISO definition of usability, a product is evaluated with respect to which three specified details?
options: Specified users, every conceivable feature, and a specified context of use
All users, specified goals, and a specified context of use
Specified users, specified goals, and specified context of use
Specified users, specified goals, and all usage scenarios
questions.explanation: The ISO usability definition is limited to specified users, specified goals, and a specified context of use.

questions.question: In usability, what does effectiveness refer to?
options: How many specified users can use the product
How fast the user can do what they want to do
Whether the user can do what they want to do
How satisfied the user is when using the system
questions.explanation: Effectiveness means whether the user can do what they want to do.

questions.question: In usability, what does efficiency refer to?
options: Whether the user can do what they want to do
How fast the user can do what they want to do
How satisfied the user is when using the system
How many specified contexts of use are supported
questions.explanation: Efficiency means how fast the user can do what they want to do.

questions.question: In usability, what does satisfaction refer to?
options: How fast the user can do what they want to do
Whether the user can do what they want to do
How well specified goals are supported
How satisfied the user is when using the system
questions.explanation: Satisfaction means how satisfied the user is when using the system.

data.text: Usability is an explicit measure of how good a system is from the point of view of the user. The ISO 9241-210-2009 standard defines usability as the extent to which a product can be used by specified users to achieve specified goals in a specified context of use. These qualities are measured through effectiveness, efficiency, and satisfaction.
points: Usability is an explicit measure of how good a system is from the point of view of the user.
The ISO 9241-210-2009 standard defines usability based on specified users, goals, and a context of use.
Usability is measured by effectiveness, efficiency, and satisfaction.

questions.question: In user-centered design, what is involved in building a usable software application?
options: Involving users actively or passively in the design or development lifecycle
Involving users only as final evaluators of the product
Involving users only after the software application is released
Involving users only through post-deployment feedback
questions.explanation: User-centered design involves users actively or passively in the design or development lifecycle used to build a usable software application.

questions.question: What is the stated objective of user-centered design?
options: To design products that increase usability
To design products for every possible context of use
To design products with every conceivable feature
To design products for every possible user
questions.explanation: The objective of user-centered design is to design products that increase usability.

questions.question: What do cooperative design, participatory design, contextual design, and human-centered design have in common?
options: They are measures of usability in a specified context of use
They are user categories chosen before a virtual tour begins
They are related terms for taking users into the design process
They are stages of the interactive system development life cycle
questions.explanation: These terms are related to user-centered design and refer to taking users into the design process.

questions.question: In user-centric software design and software development, what is the core design concern?
options: Designing usable systems that cover all possible usage scenarios
Designing usable systems that serve every possible user group
Designing usable systems that include every conceivable feature
Designing usable systems that meet lay users' needs and expectations
questions.explanation: The core design concern is the design of usable systems that cater to the needs and expectations of lay persons or layman users.

data.text: User-centered design involves users in the development lifecycle to build usable software with the objective of increasing usability. Related terms like human-centered or participatory design also refer to including users in the design process. A core concern of this approach is creating usable systems that cater to the needs and expectations of layperson users.
points: User-centered design involves users in the development lifecycle to build usable software.
The main objective of user-centered design is to increase usability.
Related terms like human-centered or participatory design also refer to including users in the design process.
Software design focuses on creating usable systems for layperson users.

questions.question: What does a user-centered software development approach require of users?
options: Involvement only after the software is released
Involvement only by expert users
Active or passive involvement in the chosen software development lifecycle
Involvement only during final testing
questions.explanation: The user-centered software development approach requires that users be actively or passively involved in the overall software development lifecycle chosen to build a system.

questions.question: Why should interaction design and user-input modeling in an XR system follow a user-centered design approach?
options: So the XR engine can use hardware resources to generate output data faster
So the output devices can stimulate the user's senses more easily
So the user can provide input data seamlessly, effectively, and easily
So the input devices can track the user's positions with less effort
questions.explanation: Interaction design and modeling of user input should follow a user-centered design approach so that the user can provide input data seamlessly, effectively, and easily.

questions.question: Why is user-centered design needed for perceptual design and modeling of output in an XR system?
options: So the input devices can track the user's positions more accurately
So the XR engine can use fewer hardware resources
So generated output stimuli match the user's perception and are easily understood
So the output devices can stimulate the user's senses with less effort
questions.explanation: Perceptual design and modeling of output requires a user-centered design approach because generated output stimuli must match the user's perception of them, so the user can perceive and understand the output easily.

questions.question: In the operation of an XR system, what is the role of the XR engine as middleware?
options: It stimulates the user's senses directly
It tracks the user's actions and positions
It collects the user's input data
It uses hardware resources to generate output data
questions.explanation: The XR engine acts as middleware that uses hardware resources to generate output data, while input devices track actions and positions and output devices stimulate the user's senses.

questions.question: Which option lists the parts that an XR system comprises?
options: Hardware, the application layer, and the user
Hardware, the XR engine as middleware, and the application layer
Input devices, output devices, and the XR engine
Hardware, the XR engine, and the user
questions.explanation: An XR system comprises hardware, the middleware that is the XR engine, and the application layer.

data.text: XR systems are highly interactive, and human factors are important to understand how users provide input and perceive output. These systems use hardware, middleware, and application layers to create a relationship between the user and the virtual environment. By applying a user-centered approach to both input interaction and output perception, developers can ensure that providing input is seamless and that output stimuli match the user's perception.
points: XR systems are highly interactive, making human factors important for understanding how users provide input and perceive output.
XR software aims to create a relationship between the user and the virtual environment using both hardware and software.
XR systems use hardware, middleware, and an application layer to track user actions and process them into output data.
Input interaction design should follow a user-centered approach to ensure that providing data is seamless, effective, and easy.
Output perception design requires a user-centered approach to ensure that generated stimuli match the user's perception.

questions.question: Why is the novice, intermittent, and expert user categorization useful at the start of interactive-system design when empirical field studies are not always practical?
questions.reference_answer: Empirical or field studies are typically needed to understand users and their behavior, but they are time-consuming, laborious, and require elaborate setup and planning, so designers can rely on the categorization instead of always starting with field studies. The categorization separates first-time, occasional, and regularly using long-term users, and because users in different classes are likely to behave differently, it provides a starting point for understanding users and making design decisions.

questions.question: Why might a word processing application provide both a menu option and a hotkey combination for the same task, such as saving a file?
questions.reference_answer: A word processing application can provide multiple options, such as a hotkey combination and a menu option, for the same task to cater to different user groups. The novice, intermittent, and expert classes consist of first-time, occasional, and regularly using long-term users, and users in different classes are likely to behave differently. The menu option takes longer but is suitable for novice first-time users because remembering hotkey combinations is generally difficult for them, while the hotkey combination may be better for intermittent users and is always preferable for expert users.

questions.question: How does user-centered design build on the user-centric approach when developing software for virtual reality or augmented reality systems?
questions.reference_answer: The user-centric approach starts by understanding user characteristics, what users need and expect, and then designing the system based on that. User-centered design results from applying this approach and involves users actively or passively in the design or development lifecycle, with the objective of increasing usability. An application software developer building virtual reality or augmented reality software therefore incorporates user characteristics by following a development or design lifecycle that accounts for users' characteristics, needs, and expectations, so the system is easier to use and better matches their needs and expectations.

questions.question: Why should an extended reality system use user-centered design for both interaction design and perceptual design?
questions.reference_answer: Extended reality systems are highly interactive, and human factors are important to understand how easily a user can provide input and perceive output. Interaction design and modeling of user input should follow user-centered design so the user can provide input data seamlessly, effectively, and easily. Perceptual design and modeling of output also requires user-centered design because output stimuli must match the user's perception so the user can perceive and understand the output easily.
